extraction.name: WikiText
extraction.description: WikiText is a language modeling benchmark dataset constructed from Wikipedia Good and Featured articles. It is available in two sizes: WikiText-2 (approximately twice the size of Penn Treebank) and WikiText-103 (over 103 million tokens). The dataset features punctuation, original casing, a larger vocabulary, and numbers, making it more realistic than the Penn Treebank for evaluating language models on rare words and long-range dependencies.
extraction.creator: Stephen Merity, Caiming Xiong, James Bradbury, Richard Socher (MetaMind - A Salesforce Company)
extraction.citeAs: Merity, S., Xiong, C., Bradbury, J., & Socher, R. (2016). Pointer Sentinel Mixture Models. arXiv:1609.07843.
extraction.rai:dataCollection: Articles were selected from Wikipedia that met the Good or Featured article criteria specified by editors. Text for each article was extracted using the Wikipedia API. Specific sections featuring lists were removed, and mathematical formulae and LaTeX code were replaced with tokens. Normalization and tokenization were performed using the Moses tokenizer.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Text extracted from Wikipedia Good and Featured articles using the Wikipedia API. This resulted in 23,805 Good articles and 4,790 Featured articles.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Specific sections featuring lists were removed. Minor bugs such as sort keys and Edit buttons were removed. Mathematical formulae and LaTeX code were replaced with tokens. Normalization and tokenization were performed using the Moses tokenizer, augmented to further split numbers. A vocabulary was constructed by discarding all words with a count below 3, with out-of-vocabulary words mapped to an <unk> token.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The Penn Treebank (a commonly compared dataset) has limitations including lower-cased tokens, stripped punctuation, and a vocabulary limited to 10k words, making it unrealistic for real language use. WikiText addresses these but the paper notes that other large-scale datasets either have restrictive licensing or randomized sentence ordering which prevents learning long-range dependencies.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: The WikiText dataset is intended for use as a language modeling benchmark, particularly for evaluating models on rare words and long-range dependencies. It is provided as training, validation, and test splits.

name.evidence: we also introduce a new benchmark dataset for language modeling called WikiText.

description.evidence: The full WikiText dataset is over 103 million words in size, a hundred times larger than the PTB... WikiText-2 is two times the size of the Penn Treebank dataset. WikiText-103 features all extracted articles. Both datasets use the same articles for validation and testing with the only difference being the vocabularies.

rai:dataCollectionRawData.evidence: We selected articles only fitting the Good or Featured article criteria specified by editors on Wikipedia. These articles have been reviewed by humans and are considered well written, factually accurate, broad in coverage, neutral in point of view, and stable. This resulted in 23,805 Good articles and 4,790 Featured articles. The text for each article was extracted using the Wikipedia API.

rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol.evidence: Once extracted, specific sections which primarily featured lists were removed by default. Other minor bugs, such as sort keys and Edit buttons that leaked in from the HTML, were also removed. Mathematical formulae and LaTeX code, were replaced with hformulai tokens. Normalization and tokenization were performed using the Moses tokenizer (Koehn et al., 2007), slightly augmented to further split numbers... Following Chelba et al. (2013) a vocabulary was constructed by discarding all words with a count below 3. Words outside of the vocabulary were mapped to the hunkitoken.

rai:machineAnnotationTools.evidence: Normalization and tokenization were performed using the Moses tokenizer (Koehn et al., 2007), slightly augmented to further split numbers (8,600 → 8 @,@ 600) and with some additional minor fixes.

rai:dataLimitations.evidence: While the processed version of the PTB above has been frequently used for language modeling, it has many limitations. The tokens in PTB are all lower case, stripped of any punctuation, and limited to a vocabulary of only 10k words. These limitations mean that the PTB is unrealistic for real language use, especially when far larger vocabularies with many rare words are involved.

rai:dataUseCases.evidence: We hope this new dataset can serve as a platform to improve handling of rare words and the usage of long term dependencies in language modeling... To ensure the dataset is immediately usable by existing language modeling tools, we have provided the dataset in the same format and following the same conventions as that of the PTB dataset above.
